caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 94 of 1995.
lawyer:
Ansarul Huque, ----- For Petitioner in person. 
Awlad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ---- For the Respondents.
parties:
Ansarul Haque ----- Petitioner
vs. 
Abdur Rahim and 4 others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ: This petition at the instance of the informant-petitioner is from judgment and order dated 2nd May, 1995 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute in Criminal Revision No. 965 of 1991 and quashing the proceeding in GR Case No. 678 of 1984 of the Court of a Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The aforesaid GR Case arose out of an First Information Report lodged by the petitioner with Gulshan PS on 15-2-84 making the respondents accused therein. The petitioner is the Managing Director of Bangal Techno Consult Ltd. and respondent No.2 is the Managing Director of Sitak Prokoushal Sangstha Ltd. and both the companies are the engineering conductors and dealers of machineries and equipment and had business transaction between themselves since 1971. In the course of such business transaction they sold to each other and purchased from each other and made payments to each other, received payments from each other in cash, by cheque and by sale of materials and equipment and services of each other's employees. In 1980 the informant's company was awarded contract of the value of US$ 3,60,982.00 for Air Conditioning of the BTV Auditorium at Rampura, Dhaka and respondent No. 2 also got a contract of value of Taka 13,60,000.00 for piping and ducting work at the same site. At that time respondent No. 1 was a clerk in the petitioner's company and was entrusted with dominion over the property of the company at BTV Auditorium construction work site. Respondent Nos. 3,4 and 5 are the employees of respondent No.2. After completion of the aforesaid Air Conditioning contract work of the BTV there was stock taking of the stores of the two companies at the work site and it is the allegation of the petitioner that huge quantity of property belonging to his company to which respondent No.1 was the custodian appeared to have been misappropriated by him by secretly making out unauthorised delivery challan in the name of the company of respondent No.2 and delivering the misappropriated property by respondent No.2 to his employees respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5. Respondent No.1 after completion of the aforesaid contract work left the service of the informant's company and joined the company of respondent No.2. The petitioner's further allegation is that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 admitted 8 items which were lodged to have been misappropriated. They returned those 8 items but denied any knowledge of the remaining 99 items of missing property. The petitioner, therefore, lodged the First Information Report alleging misappropriation of property by the respondents as alleged. The petitioner's further allegation is that the. Police recovered the property listed in the First Information Report from the possession of respondent No.2. 

 3. Police submitted charge-sheet after investigation and ultimately a Metropolitan Magistrate framed charges against all the respondents under section 408 of the Penal Code and under section 411 against respondent No. 2 on 28-4-84 in the aforesaid GR Case. 

 5. The criminal case could not proceed because of various steps taken by the respondent against the said proceeding and ultimately it appears that they came to the High Court Division in 1991 for quashing of the proceeding invoking its jurisdiction under 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. At the hearing of the matter in the High Court Division it was argued on behalf of the respondents that the dispute which cropped up between the parties subsequently after the completion of the Air Conditioning work at the BTV Auditorium was essentially a civil dispute not warranting cognisance by criminal Court. The learned Judges noticed the facts of the case as stated above and at one stage directed the learned Advocate for the respondents to file a supplementary affidavit to show whether the items shown in the schedule to the First Information Report are the same as shown in the schedule to the plaint of the petitioner, Money Suit No. 90 of 1985. The order was compliable and upon perusal of the supplementary affidavit, the learned Judges were satisfied that the criminal case and money suit were filed substantially for the same articles. It was observed that if any of the articles mentioned in the schedule to the First Information Report was not included in the schedule to the money suit, it may be included in the money suit by amending the plaint. Being of the view that in the facts and circumstances of the case the continuation of the criminal proceeding was an abuse of the process of the Court, the Rule was made absolute as already noticed. 

 6. The petitioner appeared in person with the leave of the Court and as it generally happens in a case of personal appearance, the Court hears more of emotional outpouring than legally available argument. He complained about his harassment in the hands of respondent No. 2 at one time his business colleague since taking the matter to the criminal Court in 1984 for misappropriation of property by his employees respondent in collusion with respondent No. 2. He argued that since respondent No. 1 was his servant at the relevant time and he entrusted him with the dominion of property of the petitioner's company, he could not avoid facing the criminal case for misappropriation of missing articles which were found in the possession of respondent No.1, his subsequent employer. The petitioner, however, seems to be more aggrieved because the money suits were not making any progress because of alleged obstruction by the respondents and his application for including the missing articles as per the observation of the High Court Division. The impugned judgment was allegedly turned down by the learned Subordinate Judge. 

 8. It is difficult to entertain all the grievances of the petitioner in this proceeding though one may sympathies with the predicament of the petitioner for his running about in the Courts since 1984. From the facts of the case, briefly noticed above, it appears that dispute arose between two business colleagues, petitioner and respondent No. 2, after they had worked together in installing Air Conditioning servicing at the BTV Auditorium in the beginning of 1980. There has been claim and counter-claim between the parties and admitted money suits have been filed by each of them which are pending. It cannot be said that the High Court Division was wrong in holding and acting on the premises that the dispute between the parties arising out of a joint work should be settled in the civil Court and the criminal Court should not take cognisance of such dispute. The petitioner is at liberty to include any item of property in his money suit which has been mentioned in his First Information Report and if his allegation is correct that his application for amendment of plaint for the same purpose has been rejected, he can always seek remedy in a higher Court. 

 9. The quashing of criminal proceeding, in our opinion, has not caused any miscarriage of justice in the special circumstance of this particular case.
